history.period: Ancient (mentioned in Puranas and Mahabharata) to present
history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — keep-or-drop decision needed. Triveni Sangam is the sacred confluence of the Ganga, Yamuna and the mythical Saraswati rivers, one of Hinduism's holiest bathing sites. Mythology traces the Kumbh Mela to drops of amrita falling here during the Samudra Manthan. The Purna Kumbh is held every 12 years, the Ardh Kumbh every 6 years, and the Maha Kumbh every 144 years (most recently in 2025); the annual Magh Mela is held each January-February. Emperor Ashoka erected a pillar here in the 3rd century BCE and Akbar built the Allahabad Fort adjoining it. NOTE: CSV town 'Allahabad' updated to Prayagraj (city renamed in 2018).

name: Triveni Sangam
town_description: Prayagraj (formerly Allahabad) is a major city in Uttar Pradesh at the confluence of the Ganga and Yamuna. Among India's oldest cities, it is one of the four Kumbh Mela sites, home to the Allahabad Fort, Anand Bhavan and the University of Allahabad.

travel.railway: Prayagraj Junction, ~7 km from the Sangam area
travel.road: Well connected by road; the Sangam is near Allahabad Fort on the eastern side of the city

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; January-February during the Magh Mela, or Kumbh Mela years
visitor_information.opening_hours: Open site with no fixed timings; boat rides available during daylight hours
